analysis.title: Forget The VIX: Is Tokyo Where The AI Unwind Breaks Something?
key_insights: BofA's Global Financial Stress Index (GFSI, 41 risk, skew and flow gauges) rose from +0.15 to +0.20 last week, only the 43rd percentile of weekly gains, but the move masked larger intraweek swings: +0.03 on Wednesday after the election rally, +0.17 on Thursday.

Thursday's GFSI rise coincided with falling equities and was the largest one-day rise since 10-Oct-25 (US-China trade war re-escalation). The GFSI is in its 66th percentile since 2000 and at its highest since 7-Apr. The article says this was the day the Nasdaq had its worst day since Covid.

Japan is the most stressed region by a wide margin. Japan's stress score rose 0.50 to roughly 1.7 (read off BofA's chart) versus the US up 0.06 to below 0.2. EM was flat and Europe was the only region where stress fell. Zero Hedge's napkin math puts Japan at about nine times the US.

The Nikkei fell 6% on Friday and entered a technical bear market, down 20% from its June peak, on AI-trade selling across Asia. Taiwan's Taiex also hit bear territory (per The Edge). Japan's bond futures were briefly halted.

Nikkei 3M implied vol is 31.0 (+3.5 points on the week) versus 19.2 for the S&P. KOSPI vol is above 50. Nikkei vol (+0.54) and Nikkei skew (+0.52) were the second and third biggest stress risers, behind S&P 500 skew (+0.91). Dip buyers drove volume flow as an offset.

Tibor-OIS is the most stressed of the 41 GFSI components at 2.85, ahead of S&P skew (1.94) and Nikkei implied vol (1.67). Its weekly stress jump was larger than 99% of all five-day moves since 2000, the most extreme of any gauge. Euribor-OIS was at the 98th percentile.

BofA offers no specific explanation for the Tibor-OIS spike. The article cites the backdrop: BOJ hiked in September, the October Summary of Opinions shows many members see the need for a near-term hike (December in play), Japanese investors sold a net ¥1.65 trillion of US Treasuries in September (more than triple August, per Bloomberg), and Tokyo is nudging pension funds to repatriate money.

The yen did not act as a haven: it rose only 50bps on the Nasdaq's worst day since Covid, and was not the play on Tuesday when hot CPI and Fed hawks sent the dollar to a one-month high. FX is the least stressed asset class. The article notes the Fed is pricing three hikes through 2027.
Goldman's yen-as-AI-hedge call (October 'Hedging The AI Bust') is maintained: Goldman says it needs 'a bigger and broader shift in underlying expectations than seen so far'.

Offsetting signals: broad credit stress eased, FX stress fell, and the GFSI Risk Allocator moved to a smaller underweight on risk assets (2.4% from 4.9%). The Nikkei rebounded above 60,000 on Tuesday after oil slid on US-Iran diplomacy (per Bloomberg).

Equity stress tends to fade quickly while funding stress is stickier. The article's view is that the Fed is hiking, the BOJ is about to hike into a bear market, and Japanese money is heading home as the US Treasury needs buyers, so Tokyo funding markets are the place to watch for a break.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman argues a Japan-led AI unwind is the textbook case for a yen rally and the hedge will work, but needs a bigger and broader shift in expectations than seen so far.
tension_points.bear_case: The yen rose only 50bps on the Nasdaq's worst day since Covid and was not the play on Tuesday as the dollar hit a one-month high on hot CPI and Fed hawks. The article notes the Fed is pricing three hikes through 2027, so nobody wants to stand in front of the dollar.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman says the hedge needs 'a bigger and broader shift in underlying expectations than seen so far'. The yen failing to rally even on the Nasdaq's worst day since Covid is the evidence against it.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity stress is fading: the Nikkei recovered above 60,000 on Tuesday, broad credit stress eased, and the GFSI Risk Allocator moved to a smaller underweight (2.4% from 4.9%).
tension_points.bear_case: Funding stress is stickier than equity stress. The Fed is hiking, the BOJ is about to hike into a bear market, and Japanese money is heading home just as the US Treasury needs buyers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A BOJ hike in December (the October Summary of Opinions shows many members see a near-term hike) alongside continued Japanese Treasury selling would extend the funding stress.

theme_stances.key_argument: The most stressed gauge in the 41-component index is a yen interbank spread, so Tokyo is where an AI unwind would break something.
theme_stances.evidence: we'd suggest paying less attention to the VIX and more attention to Tokyo

theme_stances.key_argument: The yen barely moved on the Nasdaq's worst day since Covid, so stress is building in Tokyo but is not being released through the currency.
